selection: Exploratory candidates from dated primary publisher reports, two weekly editorial roundups and all five weekday PTS evening-bulletin descriptions in the user-specified window. Not a national media census or a preregistered causal study.
coding: Positions are order in the written podcast synopsis, not measured broadcast running order, airtime or prominence. Oil items explicitly concern affected oils/recalls/litigation; broader food-safety policy is coded separately. Only summaries were coded, not full audio or TV programmes.
publisher: Taiwan Public Television Service; primary publisher descriptions distributed via Apple Podcasts. These are not an independent second newsroom.
coverage: All five weekday bulletin descriptions in the window; the programme describes its evening bulletins as weekday releases. No weekend TV coverage or all-day output is coded.

limitations: Dated coverage establishes competing topics existed, not that they reduced oil attention.
No impression, rating, headline-duration, platform-recommendation or same-person cross-topic browsing data are available.
Daily GA cannot identify whether a news report preceded any particular site visit within that day.
Organic Search increased on 17 July, inconsistent with a uniform simultaneous decline across all recorded channels.
Oil/food-policy items remain visible in these summaries; this does not quantify all outlets or rule out changes in total reach.
Launch publicity, promotion, day-of-week effects, referral loss and natural attention decay are competing explanations. No isolated causal effect is estimated.
